title: Armstrong gives Glaser the reins; the union deal and end of the band
summary: After the lateness Armstrong told Glaser he had full say over the band, and then the union arrangement brought Luis Russell in and let go the whole band.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: getting there. So Louis says, this is it. Mr. Glaser's got it from now on. And then, now, if you had been wanting to (intelligible) fire a guy, and tell him he's fired, and the man had cussed you out and told you what the man's going to do, and all at once the man go back and tell you, well, you got whole reins to do whatever you want to do. You got a chance, what would you do?
I don't quite follow what you mean.
Louis had a falling out with Joe? Glaser?
No, he didn't have a falling out. He didn't have a falling out. He was just letting Joe know that I wasn't fired.
Oh, I see. I see.

And he was going to be with me, if I run the band in the ground, Louis Armstrong was going in the ground with the band. Well, then he had come back to Joe and told Joe now you got full rein with the band.
Uh-huh.
Randolph and all of them.
I see.
Now, what would you do in that case? See?
Well, I don't know.
I mean, when you got a chance to. Now, here come this union, up and says, you got a band, but it look like you could -- of course, I've known things to be

pulled, where deals have been made, yeah, where they say, well, why can't you cut that down, like, I can take Louis' band in there. Because Louis' band was together, we was hitting, see. Getting down where we can get together there, and we say, and have a few standby men, stuff like that, you see. Man, can't tell what kind of deals could have been made.
I see.
Like that. But when -- if you got a chance to, you're going to abide by what the union said. And that's what happened.
Oh, really?
Yeah, oh, yeah, that's what happened.
So Glaser got rid of you?
Got rid of the whole shooting match. The whole band.
Oh, I see, with the New York --
That's how Luis Russell got in there.
Yeah.
Yeah. That's how Luis Russell got in there.
Luis Russell had the band for quite a number of years.
Yeah, he had it quite a number of years. We'd have been there quite a number of years if those boys had of acted right. But he says, he just can't do it,
Randolph, because those guys just said -- they certainly did, though. That's what they did. The boys didn't back us up. Didn't back us up one bit.
Uh-huh.
So there you go.
Well, you and Louis remained friends through the years, though, didn't you?
Oh, yes, yes, yes. We were friends right up to the end.
(End of Tape 4.)
